findings.explanation: event objects come straight from body.entry[].messaging[] (line 546-548) with no shape validation, and if fbAppSecret isn't configured verifySignature() accepts any request unauthenticated. Every other read of this same field in the file guards it with optional chaining (event.sender?.id at lines 286, 549, 552), but handleEvent reads event.sender.id directly. A messaging event without a sender object (malformed/attacker payload, or a Meta event type that omits it) throws a TypeError here, before the 'if (!senderId) return;' guard on line 647 ever gets a chance to run. It's caught by try/catch at the request-loop call sites (line 606, 632), so it doesn't crash the process, but it silently drops that event and — via the webhookQueue path (line 641 rethrows) — can drive retry/DLQ churn on every malformed event.

inferBaseUrlFromRequest() builds the base URL straight from the client-supplied X-Forwarded-Proto / X-Forwarded-Host headers with no allowlist/hostname check. The HMAC signature (verifySignature, line 265) only covers req.rawBody, not headers, so any stranger hitting POST /webhook can spoof these headers regardless of whether fbAppSecret is set. The resulting baseUrl is passed on as baseUrlOverride into getMenuImageUrls/buildRequestedImageUrls (used at lines 971-974) to construct absolute image URLs that get sent to Messenger, so a spoofed Host header lets an outside caller control the origin the bot advertises images from.
